alex (ACME): Hey folks — after yesterday's client-side rollout our similarity pipeline started failing. We get a dimension mismatch in FAISS: expected 1536, got 768. This only happened for the embeddings endpoint. Any ideas? :thinking_face:

maria (Support): Sorry you're hitting that, alex. Can you paste the exact request you send (headers + body) and a trimmed response? Also which SDK/version?

alex (ACME): here's a redacted curl (we use a project-scoped key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Our doc text","model":"embed-large-1536"}'
```

Response we see (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "model": "embed-lite-768",
  "embedding": [ /* 768 floats */ ],
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 12}
}
```

alex (ACME): note we explicitly requested "embed-large-1536" but the response is from "embed-lite-768". Downstream service fails. Billing looks charged to a different project too.

ingrid (ML Eng): interesting — two simultaneous issues: model routing and billing attribution. If the request contains a project-scoped key (proj_...) that should route to that project's default model variants unless overridden. Two quick checks: 1) which header did you include for org/project? 2) can you show the SDK version or the exact host (are you hitting a region endpoint?)

alex (ACME): we only set Authorization and Content-Type (see curl). No extra X-Org or X-Project headers. We hit api.redwood.ai (global). SDK is their internal client that just wraps curl.

maria (Support): @ingrid — this smells like a header normalization issue. We've seen cases where the client library strips custom headers and the runtime falls back to a per-org default model that is smaller (for older orgs) — resulting in the dimension change. Also billing to a different project suggests the key used might be an org-key vs project-key mismatch.

ryan (Platform): adding logs from our routing trace for alex's request-id (redacted):

```
[2026-02-12T15:40:12Z] request_id=rq_9f... auth_key_type=project key_id=proj_abc123 org_id=org_legacy_42
[2026-02-12T15:40:12Z] routing: explicit_model=embed-large-1536, model_zone=auto
[2026-02-12T15:40:12Z] policy_check: project_association=missing -> fallback to org_default_model
[2026-02-12T15:40:12Z] selected_model=embed-lite-768 (org_default)
[2026-02-12T15:40:12Z] billing_project=proj_default_01
```

ryan (Platform): TL;DR the auth key arrived without a project association in the control plane (proj_abc123 was created before project-binding was enforced) so runtime applied org_default_model and billed to the org-level default project.

alex (ACME): so the key type matters. We thought proj_abc123 was a project key. How do we force the larger model until we sort keys?

maria (Support): temporary workaround: explicitly include the model param (you already do) — but because routing occurs before model override in your case, that didn't work. Two options: 1) use an org-scoped key that has an explicit project mapping to the project you expect, or 2) add an explicit header that forces project-scoping: `X-Redwood-Project: proj_abc123` (our SDK will normalize this). Example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_abc123" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Our doc text","model":"embed-large-1536"}'
```

maria (Support): If you can't modify headers quickly, a safe mitigation is to create a new project-scoped key in the Console (Create Key -> Project -> choose desired project) and use that key — new keys are created with proper binding.

ingrid (ML Eng): added note: we introduced stricter routing checks in runtime v2.3 to avoid model-override surprises, but there are legacy keys that predate binding. We'll need to patch the control plane to retroactively map legacy keys or fallback less aggressively.

alex (ACME): ok we'll try the X-Redwood-Project header and also spin a new key. Quick question: could this cause data leakage between orgs?

ryan (Platform): short answer: no evidence of cross-org data leakage. The fallback changes model and billing target; it does not change data isolation boundaries. Still, we consider this high priority because incorrect model selection and billing are customer-impacting.

maria (Support): action items: 1) alex will try header/new key and report back; 2) we'll open internal incident so platform can map legacy keys (INC-12345); 3) engineering will add better logging to make routing reasons visible in the Console.

alex (ACME): update — we created a new project key and the explicit header. New request shows: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "model": "embed-large-1536",
  "embedding": [ /* 1536 floats */ ],
  "vector_length": 1536
}
```

alex (ACME): Verified downstream service no longer errors. Billing now reflects the expected project. Thank you. :raised_hands:

ryan (Platform): great. We'll keep INC-12345 open and follow up with a control-plane patch to auto-map legacy keys or surface a warning in the Console when an unbound key is used. Expect an update in 48 hours.

maria (Support): thanks — will post updates here. :eyes:
